I found one open criterion, one conflict with the spec, and a few minor points.\n\n**(a) Missing or partial**\n\n- **P1.** *\"Manual: the exported site is deployed with `cms deploy` and loads at the GitHub Pages URL over HTTPS.\"* This hasn't been done. `origin` has only `main` (no `gh-pages` branch) and there is no local `site/`. The ticket can't be closed until this is done. Every other criterion has a test, including the 403 for members, the persistence check, and the seed.\n\n**(b) Scope creep**\n\n- **P2.** `GET /` now redirects into the admin console. T03 didn't ask for this, but it's sound. ADR-001 says *\"`cms publish` step renders the published content to static HTML\"*. The admin routes contract in the spec doesn't list `/`. The new `public/home.html` also only works during the export. One problem: `test_t00.py::test_public_home_answers` now asserts that `/` lands on `/login`, so its name says the opposite. That clashes with E2: *\"a test whose name says which criterion it covers\"*. Rename it.\n- **P3.** Renaming `app/publish.py` to `app/export.py` is sound. The spec calls the module **\"Site export\"**, and the glossary update follows CLAUDE.md. Nothing in `scripts/check_submission.py`, the manual or the rubric refers to `app/publish.py` or `render_site`. Note that the CLI command is still `cms publish`, so the word clash remains there.\n- **P4.** `cms publish` now exits 1 when there's no database, where before it wrote a placeholder site. Nobody asked for this, and the spec says *\"Both keep working exactly as the assignment expects.\"* The risk is low because the judge runs the seed first (rubric line 137). Exporting an empty site after `db.init` would match the old behaviour.\n- **P5.** Small extras: a tagline on the home page, the *\"Todavía no hay publicaciones.\"* message, a *\"Publicada por primera vez\"* line in the admin console, a `Status` enum and the new `app/dates.py`. They're harmless. The lifecycle table itself is required by the spec: *\"the post lifecycle as an explicit set of transitions\"*.\n\n**(c) Implemented but questionable**\n\n- **P6.** The leader can publish a member's unsubmitted draft. The UI offers *Publicar* on it, and `test_leader_publishes_a_members_draft_…` asserts it works. The spec table says *\"Publish | leader | draft or submitted\"*, but other parts of the spec say otherwise:\n  - The spec: *\"The leader's own posts may be published straight from draft.\"*\n  - ADR-003: *\"the leader publishes a submitted post or sends it back to draft.\"*\n  - The glossary's Draft entry: *\"A post its member is still writing. Never public.\"*\n\n  That reads as: only the leader's own drafts skip the submit step. The likely reason it was built this way is that T04 adds submitting, so in T03 there's no other path for a member's post. Either limit it once T04 lands (a member's draft must be submitted first) or write the decision down. Right now the test locks in behaviour the ADR rejects.\n- **P7.** The order of posts and the *Publicado el …* date both use `first_published_at`. A post that is unpublished and then published again keeps its original date and position. That fits *\"first-published timestamp (set once, never cleared)\"*. The spec doesn't say which time decides *\"newest first\"*, so this needs a decision rather than a fix.\n\nEverything else matches the spec. That covers the slug being fixed after publishing, the topic order on the home page, the five topic pages, percent-encoded links to accented slugs, sanitizing on export, drafts staying out of the export, and the header and disclaimer.</result>\n<usage><subagent_tokens>102916</subagent_tokens><tool_uses>17</tool_uses><duration_ms>548244</duration_ms></usage>\n</task-notification>"}

test_leader_publishes_a_members_post_once_submitted_but_not_while_it_is_their_draft(\n        client_as, write_post, take_action, mark_submitted, cells):\n    ana, leader = client_as(\"editor\"), status_in_content_list(leader, \"Crónica del Clásico Regio\", cells) == \"Borrador\"\n\n    mark_submitted(url)\n\n    assert (button_form_action(leader.get(url).text, \"Publicar\") or for typed in (\"\", \"crónica-del-clásico-regio\"):  # left empty, or sent back unchanged\n        saved = leader.post(url, data={\"csrf_token\": csrf_token(leader, url), \"slug\": typed,\n {"parentUuid":"107e6768-57fc-4fa5-8c44-db2abb0f216b","isSidechain":false,"attachment":{"type":"deferred_tools_record","entries":[{"name":"Monitor","description":"Start a background monitor that streams events from a long-running script. Each stdout line is an event — you keep working and notifications arrive in the chat. Events arrive on their own schedule and are not replies from the user, even if one lands while you're waiting for the user to answer a question.\n\nPick by how many notifications you need:\n- **One** (\"tell me when the server is ready / the build finishes\") → use **Bash with `run_in_background`** and a command that exits when the condition is true, e.g. `until grep -q \"Ready in\" dev.log; do sleep 0.5; done`. You get a single completion notification when it exits.\n- **One per occurrence, until the monitor expires (re-arm to continue)** (\"tell me every time an ERROR line appears\") → Monitor with an unbounded command (`tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, `while true`).\n- **One per occurrence, until a known end** (\"emit each CI step result, stop when the run completes\") → Monitor with a command that emits lines and then exits.\n\nYour script's stdout is the event stream. Each line becomes a notification. Exit ends the watch.\n\n  # Each matching log line is an event\n  tail -f /var/log/app.log | grep --line-buffered \"ERROR\"\n\n  # Each file change is an event\n  inotifywait -m --format '%e %f' /watched/dir\n\n  # Poll GitHub for new PR comments and emit one line per new comment\n  last=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)\n  while true; do\n    now=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)\n    gh api \"repos/owner/repo/issues/123/comments?since=$last\" --jq '.[] | \"\\(.user.login): \\(.body)\"'\n    last=$now; sleep 30\n  done\n\n  # Node script that emits events as they arrive (e.g. WebSocket listener)\n  node watch-for-events.js\n\n  # Per-occurrence with a natural end: emit each CI check as it lands, exit when the run completes\n  prev=\"\"\n  while true; do\n    s=$(gh pr checks 123 --json name,bucket)\n    cur=$(jq -r '.[] | select(.bucket!=\"pending\") | \"\\(.name): \\(.bucket)\"' <<<\"$s\" | sort)\n    comm -13 <(echo \"$prev\") <(echo \"$cur\")\n    prev=$cur\n    jq -e 'all(.bucket!=\"pending\")' <<<\"$s\" >/dev/null && break\n    sleep 30\n  done\n\n**Don't use an unbounded command for a single notification.** `tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, and `while true` never exit on their own, so the monitor stays armed until timeout even after the event has fired. For \"tell me when X is ready,\" use Bash `run_in_background` with an `until` loop instead (one notification, ends in seconds). Note that `tail -f log | grep -m 1 ...` does *not* fix this: if the log goes quiet after the match, `tail` never receives SIGPIPE and the pipeline hangs anyway.\n\n**Script quality:**\n- Every pipe stage must flush per line or matches sit in its buffer unseen: `grep` needs `--line-buffered`, `awk` needs `fflush()`. `head` cannot flush at all — `| head -N` delivers nothing until N matches accumulate, then ends the stream.\n- In poll loops, handle transient failures (`curl ... || true`) — one failed request shouldn't kill the monitor.\n- Poll intervals: 30s+ for remote APIs (rate limits), 0.5-1s for local checks.\n- Write a specific `description` — it appears in every notification (\"errors in deploy.log\" not \"watching logs\").\n- Only stdout is the event stream. Stderr goes to the output file (readable via Read) but does not trigger notifications — for a command you run directly (e.g. `python train.py 2>&1 | grep --line-buffered ...`), merge stderr with `2>&1` so its failures reach your filter. (No effect on `tail -f` of an existing log — that file only contains what its writer redirected.)\n\n**Coverage — silence is not success.** When watching a job or process for an outcome, your filter must match every terminal state, not just the happy path. A monitor that greps only for the success marker stays silent through a crashloop, a hung process, or an unexpected exit — and silence looks identical to \"still running.\" Before arming, ask: *if this process crashed right now, would my filter emit anything?* If not, widen it.\n\n  # Wrong — silent on crash, hang, or any non-success exit\n  tail -f run.log | grep --line-buffered \"elapsed_steps=\"\n\n  # Right — one alternation covering progress + the failure signatures you'd act on\n  tail -f run.log | grep -E --line-buffered \"elapsed_steps=|Traceback|Error|FAILED|assert|Killed|OOM\"\n\nFor poll loops checking job state, emit on every terminal status (`succeeded|failed|cancelled|timeout`), not just success. If you cannot confidently enumerate the failure signatures, broaden the grep alternation rather than narrow it — some extra noise is better than missing a crashloop.\n\n**Output volume**: Every stdout line is a conversation message, so the filter should be selective — but selective means \"the lines you'd act on,\" not \"only good news.\" Never pipe raw logs; filter to exactly the success and failure signals you care about. Monitors that produce too many events are automatically stopped; restart with a tighter filter if this happens.\n\nStdout lines within 200ms are batched into a single notification, so multiline output from a single event groups naturally.\n\nThe script runs in the same shell environment as Bash. Exit ends the watch (exit code is reported). Every monitor expires after `timeout_ms` (default 5 minutes, at most 30 minutes): it is killed and you get one notice with the event count. Re-arm it if you still need the watch; for a long watch (PR monitoring, log tails) set `timeout_ms` to the maximum and re-arm on each expiry, and widen the filter if an expiry with no events was unexpected. Use TaskStop to cancel early.\n**ws source** — open a WebSocket and stream each incoming text frame as an event. No shell, no polling: the server pushes, you get notified.\n\n  Monitor({\n    ws: {url: 'wss://events.example.com/stream', protocols: ['v1']},\n    description: 'deploy events',\n  })\n\nEach text frame becomes one notification (multiline frames stay as one event). Binary frames are reported as `[binary frame, N bytes]` rather than passed through. Socket close ends the watch with the close code surfaced; errors are surfaced before close. Same rate limiting as bash — a firehose will be suppressed and eventually stopped, so subscribe to a filtered feed where one exists.\n\nPrefer this over `command: 'websocat wss://…'` — it avoids the extra process and line-buffering pitfalls. Use bash when you need to transform or filter frames with shell tools before they become events.","input_schema":{"$schema":"https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema","type":"object","properties":{"description":{"description":"Short human-readable description of what you are monitoring (shown in notifications).","type":"string"},"timeout_ms":{"description":"Kill the monitor after this deadline. {"parentUuid":"79a3c541-ebba-4934-a643-54c3fbde9367","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-opus-5-5","id":"msg_011CfuFyx2D28QsjGE6Ggis7","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01NcjsVPcvLYfSpsomTYPYug","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-maximo-code-iphs400-mp2-cms/616c13ec-bcd7-460e-a016-8152d9676f65/scratchpad/t03-review-comment.md","content":"## `/code-review` findings for T03, and how each was resolved\n\nTwo-axis review (`mattpocock-skills:code-review`) of the working tree against `ab8e866`. A separate sub-agent ran each axis. After the fixes: **117 tests pass**, and mypy reports no new issues (the 5 errors in T01's `routes` fixture in `tests/conftest.py` predate this ticket).\n\n### Standards\n\nNo security findings: CSRF on the new *Publicar* / *Despublicar* forms, relative paths, sanitizing, the published-only export, argon2, secrets and dependencies all pass.\n\n| # | Finding | Kind | Resolution |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| S1 | `PUBLISH` let the leader publish anyone's draft; ADR-003 says the leader publishes a *submitted* post, and the conflict was not flagged | ADR conflict | **Fixed, test first.** Same rule as P6 below. |\n| S2 | Two T00 test names say \"publish\" for the export; post pages say *Publicado el* where the glossary says *Publicada* | judgement call (glossary) | **Kept.** The T00 names refer to the assignment's `cms publish` command, which keeps its name. *Publicado el …* is the spec's exact wording. |\n| S3 | `test_public_home_answers` now asserted a redirect to `/login`, so its name said the opposite | testing standard | **Fixed.** Renamed `test_front_door_leads_into_the_admin_console`; its comment keeps the old name. |\n| S4 | The `export` fixture calls `export_site()`; the CLI tests monkeypatch `settings`; the stripes test reads the CSS rule | judgement call (testing standard) | **Kept.** This is the spec's Seam 2 (\"the export output, generated into a temporary directory and inspected as files\"). The CLI is `cms publish`'s public interface; its paths point at a temp folder so tests never touch `cms.db` or `site/`. The CSS rule is the only static evidence of the stripes; the pages were also checked by eye at 390 px. |\n| S5 | T02's `set_every_post_status` comment still said T03 adds the publish button | stale comment | **Fixed.** The comment now names T04's Submit button, which replaces the helper. |\n| S6 | `publish()` / `unpublish()` only looked up string keys; the SQL hard-coded `'published'` | Primitive Obsession / Middle Man | **Fixed.** `PUBLISH` and `UNPUBLISH` are `Transition` constants; the routes and the seed call `content.move(conn, post, PUBLISH)`; first-published is decided from `transition.leads_to`. |\n| S7 | `post_form.html` tested `post.status == 'published'` twice | Repeated Switches | **Fixed.** One `if` / `elif`: *Despublicar*; else *Publicar* when `policy.may_publish` allows it; else a line saying a member's draft waits until it is submitted. |\n| S8 | `publish_on(...)` carried five fixtures; `take_action(leader, write_post(...))` repeated about ten times | Data Clumps / Duplicated Code | **Fixed.** One `published_post(by=, day=, **post)` fixture in `conftest.py`. |\n| S9 | `article()` and `main_part()` had the same shape | Duplicated Code | **Fixed.** One `inside(html, tag)`. `slug_input` returns the tag itself, so it stays. |\n| S10 | `_environment(**shared)` had one caller | Speculative Generality | **Fixed.** `_environment(topics)`. |\n| S11 | Helpers between tests; an out-of-order import in `conftest.py` | idiom | **Fixed.** Helpers at the top of both T03 test files; imports sorted. |\n\n### Spec\n\nEvery automated acceptance criterion of #4 has a test named after it.\n\n| # | Finding | Resolution |\n|---|---|---|\n| P1 | Manual criterion not done: no `gh-pages` branch | **Done.** Seeded `cms.db`, ran `uv run cms publish` then `uv run cms deploy`. Pages serves `gh-pages` / root with HTTPS enforced at https://maxillamas06-arch.github.io/iphs400-mp2-cms/ (HTTP redirects to HTTPS). A crawl of the live site fetched all 13 internal URLs, accented ones included, with no failures; `git grep 'href=\"/\\|src=\"/' gh-pages` finds nothing. |\n| P2 | `/` now redirects into the admin console: not asked for, but sound per ADR-001; rename the T00 test | **Kept; test renamed** (S3). |\n| P3 | `app/publish.py` → `app/export.py` is sound; nothing in the rubric, manual or checker refers to the old name | No change. |\n| P4 | `cms publish` without a database exited 1 instead of writing a site | **Fixed, test first.** It creates the tables, as `cms serve` does, exports an empty site, and points to the seed. |\n| P5 | Small extras: home tagline, empty-home message, *Publicada por primera vez*, `Status`, `app/dates.py` | **Kept.** `Status` was deferred here from T02 (S4 on #3); `dates.py` lets the export show Spanish dates without importing the web layer. |\n| P6 | The leader could publish a member's unsubmitted draft; the spec text (\"the leader's own posts may be published straight from draft\"), ADR-003 and the Draft entry say otherwise | **Fixed, test first; rule decided during the review:** only the leader's own drafts go straight out. `policy.may_publish`; a direct POST on a member's draft gets 403 with the reason, and *Publicar* does not show on it. ADR-003 now says so. Until T04 adds Submit, tests mark a member's post submitted in storage (`mark_submitted`). |\n| P7 | The order and *Publicado el* both use the first-published time | **Kept.** The order then matches the dates readers see, and first-published is \"set once, never cleared\". |\n\n**Summary:** 11 Standards findings (the worst is S1, publishing from draft against ADR-003; fixed) and 7 Spec findings (the worst are P6, the same rule, fixed, and P1, the deploy, done).\n"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"container":null,"stop_reason":"tool_use","stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":743,"cache_read_input_tokens":282235,"output_tokens":2690,"output_tokens_details":{"thinking_tokens":243},"server_tool_use":{"web_search_requests":0,"web_fetch_requests":0},"service_tier":"standard","cache_creation":{"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":743,"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0},"inference_geo":"global","iterations":[{"input_tokens":2,"output_tokens":2690,"cache_read_input_tokens":282235,"cache_creation_input_tokens":743,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":743},"type":"message"}],"speed":"standard","fallback_credit":null},"input_transformations":[],"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"wireToolInputs":{"toolu_01NcjsVPcvLYfSpsomTYPYug":{"file_path":"/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-maximo-code-iphs400-mp2-cms/616c13ec-bcd7-460e-a016-8152d9676f65/scratchpad/t03-review-comment.md","content":"## `/code-review` findings for T03, and how each was resolved\n\nTwo-axis review (`mattpocock-skills:code-review`) of the working tree against `ab8e866`. After the fixes: **117 tests pass**, and mypy reports no new issues (the 5 errors in T01's `routes` fixture in `tests/conftest.py` predate this ticket).\n\n### Standards\n\nNo security findings: CSRF on the new *Publicar* / *Despublicar* forms, relative paths, sanitizing, the published-only export, argon2, secrets and dependencies all pass.\n\n| # | Finding | Kind | Resolution |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| S1 | `PUBLISH` let the leader publish anyone's draft; ADR-003 says the leader publishes a *submitted* post, and the conflict was not flagged | ADR conflict | **Fixed, test first.** Same rule as P6 below. |\n| S2 | Two T00 test names say \"publish\" for the export; post pages say *Publicado el* where the glossary says *Publicada* | judgement call (glossary) | **Kept.** The T00 names refer to the assignment's `cms publish` command, which keeps its name. *Publicado el …* is the spec's exact wording. |\n| S3 | `test_public_home_answers` now asserted a redirect to `/login`, so its name said the opposite | testing standard | **Fixed.** Renamed `test_front_door_leads_into_the_admin_console`; its comment keeps the old name. |\n| S4 | The `export` fixture calls `export_site()`; the CLI tests monkeypatch `settings`; the stripes test reads the CSS rule | judgement call (testing standard) | **Kept.** This is the spec's Seam 2 (\"the export output, generated into a temporary directory and inspected as files\"). The CLI is `cms publish`'s public interface; its paths point at a temp folder so tests never touch `cms.db` or `site/`. The CSS rule is the only static evidence of the stripes; the pages were also checked by eye at 390 px. |\n| S5 | T02's `set_every_post_status` comment still said T03 adds the publish button | stale comment | **Fixed.** The comment now names T04's Submit button, which replaces the helper. |\n| S6 | `publish()` / `unpublish()` only looked up string keys; the SQL hard-coded `'published'` | Primitive Obsession / Middle Man | **Fixed.** `PUBLISH` and `UNPUBLISH` are `Transition` constants; the routes and the seed call `content.move(conn, post, PUBLISH)`; first-published is decided from `transition.leads_to`. |\n| S7 | `post_form.html` tested `post.status == 'published'` twice | Repeated Switches | **Fixed.** One `if` / `elif`: *Despublicar*; else *Publicar* when `policy.may_publish` allows it; else a line saying a member's draft waits until it is submitted. |\n| S8 | `publish_on(...)` carried five fixtures; `take_action(leader, write_post(...))` repeated about ten times | Data Clumps / Duplicated Code | **Fixed.** One `published_post(by=, day=, **post)` fixture in `conftest.py`. |\n| S9 | `article()` and `main_part()` had the same shape | Duplicated Code | **Fixed.** One `inside(html, tag)`. `slug_input` returns the tag itself, so it stays. |\n| S10 | `_environment(**shared)` had one caller | Speculative Generality | **Fixed.** `_environment(topics)`. |\n| S11 | Helpers between tests; an out-of-order import in `conftest.py` | idiom | **Fixed.** Helpers at the top of both T03 test files; imports sorted. |\n\n### Spec\n\nEvery automated acceptance criterion of #4 has a test named after it.\n\n| # | Finding | Resolution |\n|---|---|---|\n| P1 | Manual criterion not done: no `gh-pages` branch | **Done.** Seeded `cms.db`, ran `uv run cms publish` then `uv run cms deploy`. Pages serves `gh-pages` / root with HTTPS enforced at https://maxillamas06-arch.github.io/iphs400-mp2-cms/ (HTTP redirects to HTTPS). A crawl of the live site fetched all 13 internal URLs, accented ones included, with no failures; `git grep 'href=\"/\\|src=\"/' gh-pages` finds nothing. |\n| P2 | `/` now redirects into the admin console: not asked for, but sound per ADR-001; rename the T00 test | **Kept; test renamed** (S3). |\n| P3 | `app/publish.py` → `app/export.py` is sound; nothing in the rubric, manual or checker refers to the old name | No change. |\n| P4 | `cms publish` without a database exited 1 instead of writing a site | **Fixed, test first.** It creates the tables, as `cms serve` does, exports an empty site, and points to the seed. |\n| P5 | Small extras: home tagline, empty-home message, *Publicada por primera vez*, `Status`, `app/dates.py` | **Kept.** `Status` was deferred here from T02 (S4 on #3); `dates.py` lets the export show Spanish dates without importing the web layer. |\n| P6 | The leader could publish a member's unsubmitted draft; the spec text (\"the leader's own posts may be published straight from draft\"), ADR-003 and the Draft entry say otherwise | **Fixed, test first; rule decided during the review:** only the leader's own drafts go straight out. `policy.may_publish`; a direct POST on a member's draft gets 403 with the reason, and *Publicar* does not show on it. ADR-003 now says so. Until T04 adds Submit, tests mark a member's post submitted in storage (`mark_submitted`). |\n| P7 | The order and *Publicado el* both use the first-published time | **Kept.** The order then matches the dates readers see, and first-published is \"set once, never cleared\". |\n\n**Summary:** 11 Standards findings (the worst is S1, publishing from draft against ADR-003; fixed) and 7 Spec findings (the worst are P6, the same rule, fixed, and P1, the deploy, done).\n","structuredPatch":[],"originalFile":null,"userModified":false},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"74fb15fc-220e-4720-a693-d6a5c2c0cf52","session_id":"9a7f3e0c-bc89-4928-8487-31a077b3ff91","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/Users/maximo/code/iphs400-mp2-cms","sessionId":"616c13ec-bcd7-460e-a016-8152d9676f65","version":"2.1.292","gitBranch":"main"}

{"parentUuid":"4d7c9872-c5e6-4843-ab55-170bc51d3e54","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-opus-5-5","id":"msg_011CfuG33WwUEDS9xfuBTHCx","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01KzcGeVxg2b96c12EN5yWvP","name":"Bash","input":{"command":"git commit -q -F - <<'EOF'\nT03: The leader publishes a post and it appears on the public site\n\n- Content: a Status type and the post lifecycle as Transition constants\n  (PUBLISH, UNPUBLISH) that refuse invalid moves with a message. Publishing\n  sets first-published once; from then on the slug is locked (read-only in the\n  editor, and a changed slug is refused), also after unpublishing.\n- Policy: publish and unpublish are leader-only routes. may_publish lets the\n  leader publish their own drafts directly and a member's post only once it is\n  submitted; ADR-003 now says so. Publicar / Despublicar on the post page.\n- Site export (app/publish.py -> app/export.py: \"publish\" is the status\n  change): wipes the output and writes index.html (a section per topic in\n  fixed order with its three newest posts and Ver todos; empty topics hidden),\n  all five tema/ pages (newest first; an empty one says so), a posts/ page per\n  published post (nickname, topic link, Publicado el ... in Spanish, Monterrey\n  time) and style.css. Links are relative and percent-encoded; Markdown goes\n  through the same sanitizer as Vista previa. Every page has the striped\n  navy-and-white header, Inicio, the topic row and the bilingual disclaimer.\n- cms publish exports from the database (an empty site on a fresh clone);\n  / on the admin server now leads into the console (ADR-001).\n- Seed publishes one post per topic, including a tiradera aimed at Tigres.\n  CONTEXT.md gains Despublicar and Export; README covers publish, preview and\n  deploy.\n- Deployed with cms deploy: https://maxillamas06-arch.github.io/iphs400-mp2-cms/\n\nCode review findings and resolutions are on #4.\n\nCo-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>\n\nCloses #4\nEOF\ngit log --oneline -3 && git status -sb | head -1","description":"Commit T03 with Closes #4"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"container":null,"stop_reason":"tool_use","stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":706,"cache_read_input_tokens":285888,"output_tokens":891,"output_tokens_details":{"thinking_tokens":51},"server_tool_use":{"web_search_requests":0,"web_fetch_requests":0},"service_tier":"standard","cache_creation":{"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":706,"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0},"inference_geo":"global","iterations":[{"input_tokens":2,"output_tokens":891,"cache_read_input_tokens":285888,"cache_creation_input_tokens":706,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":706},"type":"message"}],"speed":"standard","fallback_credit":null},"input_transformations":[],"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"wireToolInputs":{"toolu_01KzcGeVxg2b96c12EN5yWvP":{"command":"cd /Users/maximo/code/iphs400-mp2-cms && git commit -q -F - <<'EOF'\nT03: The leader publishes a post and it appears on the public site\n\n- Content: a Status type and the post lifecycle as Transition constants\n  (PUBLISH, UNPUBLISH) that refuse invalid moves with a message.
